provenance.description: The commands and test results below were executed previously and reported through tool output. This JSON records those existing results; it is not a new raw test log.
current_record_actions: Read-only SHA-256 and size verification of the frozen v2 wheel, isolated unpacked pyd, and current Rust source files.

historical_executions.purpose: Rust release-mode unit tests, including exact subgroup and exponentiation oracles
Native verifier, Python adapter, malicious partial-decryption, and service integration regressions against the isolated v2 module
Lint the native verifier regression test file

oracle_coverage.membership_value_construction: Five fixed values plus 32 seeded groups of four values: general Fq12, unitary non-cyclotomic, cyclotomic non-q-order, and valid q-order GT.
oracle_coverage.unitary_fixture: u = Frob6(x) / x; explicitly checked unitary and not cyclotomic
oracle_coverage.cyclotomic_non_q_fixture: c = Frob2(u) * u; explicitly checked cyclotomic and ordinary c^q != 1
oracle_coverage.public_variable_base_exponent_oracle: 32 seeded valid GT/public scalar pairs and boundary exponents 0, 1, q-1, and bit 254 compared exactly with ordinary Fq12 power
oracle_coverage.public_fixed_base_table_oracle: Exact comparison with ordinary exponentiation for 0, 1, 15, 16, 255, 256, bit 254, q-1, and q-1234567

regression_coverage: Canonical G1, GT, and scalar decoding; malformed lengths and off-subgroup values.
Unitary but non-cyclotomic GT and cyclotomic but non-q-order GT rejected as T, B, and E through the native adapter; unmodified NativeGT decoder supplies an independent q-order oracle.
Wrong trusted DKG anchor, G/H/T binding, challenge, A, B, E, and each response rejected.
Opaque polynomial handle cannot be constructed or pickled; cross-verifier rebinding rejected.
Legacy valid proof equations remain compatible.
Adapter cache hit rechecks changed trusted constants; list[int] substituted for wire point or scalar rejected.
Dimension 65 exercises the parallel branch for workers 1, 2, and 4, including tampering in the last coordinate.
An authorized signer changing its E to alter aggregate 17 to 7 is rejected.
Self-consistent fake verification keys, forged identical D, and polynomial equivocation rejected against trusted DKG anchors; honest alternate cloud pair accepted.
Signed malicious service results rejected across all four client proof suites without finishing the round; a subsequent honest finish succeeds.

security_boundaries.canonical_decoding: Wire field elements and scalars retain exact length, canonical encoding, and round-trip checks; Python adapter additionally enforces bytes-like types.
security_boundaries.gt_membership: For canonical nonzero x, Frob4(x) * x == Frob2(x) establishes membership in Phi12(p); cyclotomic_exp(Fr::MODULUS) == 1 then separately establishes q-order subgroup membership.
security_boundaries.public_exponent_only: Cyclotomic exponentiation and centered-exponent conjugate inversion are used only in public verification for already subgroup-checked E and a public challenge. The fixed T table is used only for public response exponents.
security_boundaries.equations: Both G1 and GT proof equations are checked for every coordinate. No random residual aggregation or equation omission is introduced.
security_boundaries.trust_binding: Opaque polynomial handles bind the verifier G/H/T and checked DKG constant commitments; Python context, signatures, Fiat-Shamir challenge, authorized membership, and cache-hit anchor checks remain required.

review_and_limitations.review: Independent internal static review checked the Frobenius subgroup gate, subsequent q-order test, and public-only exponentiation domain; no blocking issue was reported.
review_and_limitations.primary_math_reference_title: Granger and Scott, Faster Squaring in the Cyclotomic Subgroup of Sixth Degree Extensions, section 3
review_and_limitations.performance_note: This acceptance record makes no v2 performance claim. Parent-controlled full-role benchmarks are separate evidence.
review_and_limitations.scope: Isolated native cryptographic acceptance and adapter/integration regressions; this JSON does not substitute for whole-project acceptance.
